question: Can a normal GTK2 theme engine add the two horizontal terminal caps and set caret height to the VUE measurement without patching GTK or replacing application widgets?

findings.gtkstyle.c: gtk_draw_insertion_cursor is documented in source as a convenience function, explicitly not a style function. It calculates width from cursor-aspect-ratio and draws the stem plus optional bidi arrow; it does not draw horizontal end caps.
findings.gtkentry.c: GtkEntry calls gtk_draw_insertion_cursor directly (line 5688 in the installed source copy).
findings.gtktextdisplay.c: GtkTextView calls the same helper directly (line 894 in the installed source copy).
findings.gtkstyle.h: The public GtkStyleClass exposes drawing callbacks for boxes, lines, arrows, checks, and other primitives, but no insertion-cursor callback. A theme engine therefore has no ordinary style vfunc to override for this caret.
findings.height: The caret height is supplied by the Entry/TextView text-layout geometry. The theme style property affects width, not the height or cap shape.

conclusion: GTK2 theme files or a conventional GtkThemeEngine cannot provide exact VUE caret terminals or force only this caret to 14px while preserving application text metrics. That would require changing GTK2's helper or replacing/subclassing the text widget in each application. No toolkit patch or application-specific widget was made.
existing_theme_adaptation: Keep the R61 cursor-aspect-ratio=0.0 setting: it gives a 1px stem and follows the current KDE text role. R61 measured 18px height at 338x34, while SR10.4 measured 14px plus two 5x1px terminals.
method: Read-only source inspection and comparison of public GtkStyleClass declarations with the direct GtkEntry and GtkTextView helper call sites. No GUI, VM, toolkit installation, or user configuration changed.
remaining: Historical color, selected-text shape, and caret blink timing remain unmeasured in SR10.4.
The GTK2 adapter still lacks a real mapped-window focus-cycle observation in an isolated target.
